author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-4 -->
Principal ruling, round 4. §4 is amended to include `packages/aeg-core/src/verdict-extraction.ts`. One commit, four items. Every item below is backed by a command run against this branch before ruling.

**Evidence**

```
$ grep -n -A1 "^export function deriveCodeReviewVerdict" apps/cli/src/commands/review-post.ts
191:export function deriveCodeReviewVerdict(findings: readonly Finding[]): CodeReviewVerdict {
192:  return findings.some((f) => f.severity === 'BLOCKER') ? 'REQUEST_CHANGES' : 'APPROVE'
$ grep -n "fix-claimed" apps/cli/src/commands/review-post.ts
543:const FINDING_DESCRIPTION_ID = /^F(\d+)\s+\S+(?:\s+(open|fix-claimed|reproduced|resolved))?:/
$ grep -n "git', \['diff'" apps/cli/src/commands/review-post.ts
827:    out = execFileSync('git', ['diff', `${judgedHead}...HEAD`, '-U0'], {
$ grep -n "/im" packages/aeg-core/src/verdict-extraction.ts
88:const HEAD_SHA_PATTERN = /^[ \t]*(?:\*{1,3}|_{1,3})?Judged head:\s*([0-9a-f]{7,40})(?![A-Za-z0-9])/im
128:    /^[ \t]*(?:\*{1,3}|_{1,3})?VERDICT:\s*(APPROVE|REQUEST[ _-]?CHANGES|LGTM)(?![A-Za-z0-9])/im,
137:    /^[ \t]*(?:\*{1,3}|_{1,3})?VERDICT:\s*(PASS|FAIL)(?![A-Za-z0-9])/im,
$ probe: escalation comment with "verdict: PASS" inside a fence, through extractSecurityReviewVerdict
security: {"value":"PASS","headSha":"2332a6ea…"}
```

**Ruling**

1. `verdict-extraction.ts`: `VERDICT:` and `Judged head:` are matched against a comment's first three lines only. Two existing fixtures place the verdict deeper (`underscore-emphasized`, `regression 5`); move their verdict line to line 1, they test decoration, not position. Test: a verdict on line 4, inside a fence, or in lowercase prose extracts as no verdict.
2. `review-post.ts`: delete `fieldsContainingVerdict` and the newline guard. Before any `gh` call, run both extractors over the rendered comment; refuse unless exactly the intended verdict extracts and the other role extracts none. Multi-line fields are then safe; add `--scope-evidence-file`, rendered as a fenced block below the verdict block.
3. `deriveCodeReviewVerdict` and `deriveSecurityVerdict`: a finding whose state is `resolved` never counts. One clause in each role doc: a resolved prior id keeps its original severity for the record and never drives the verdict.
4. `computeChangedRanges`: `git fetch origin <resolvedHead>` then diff `<judgedHead>...<resolvedHead>`; refuse if either is absent locally.

Changeset: `@attalabs/aeg-core` patch, `@attalabs/vinaya` minor. The `pr-body-frozen` red on this PR is a stale webhook body, not a hand edit; an empty commit clears it. Then one comment `Head: <sha>`, and stop.

1. [HIGH] packages/aeg-core/src/verdict-extraction.ts:133 — F3 other:gate-fail-open: the new three-line read window makes the merge gate fail OPEN in the one case it was designed to fail closed - a later blocking verdict superseding an earlier clean one at the same head. `extractVerdict` now builds `clearHits` from `firstThreeLines(c)` (line 133), so a principal-authored comment whose `VERDICT:` marker sits on line 4 or below is not merely unbound, it is absent from the candidate set entirely; most-recent-clear-hit-wins then hands the gate the EARLIER comment. Reproduced by direct execution against the head build of this exact file (2db38683, no re-implementation): comment A = the command's own render `VERDICT: PASS` / blank / `Judged head: 2db38683...`; comment B, posted later by the same allowlisted author at the same head, opening with this repo's own established HTML-anchor-plus-heading shape (`<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-4 -->` and `<!-- aeg:body-hash:... -->` are both already on this PR) so `VERDICT: FAIL` lands on line 5. `extractSecurityReviewVerdict([B])` returns the DANGLING placeholder; `extractSecurityReviewVerdict([A, B])` returns `{value: "PASS", headSha: "2db38683...", danglingNote: null}` - clean and bound to the CURRENT head, so `checkReviewGate` returns verdict `pass` while a live same-head FAIL carrying a CRITICAL stands on the PR. author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-5 -->
Principal ruling, round 5, on the security HIGH at #issuecomment-5522065460 (head `2db38683`). The finding stands; the fix stays inside round 4.

```
$ git show origin/task/review-convergence-v1/2:packages/aeg-core/src/verdict-extraction.ts | sed -n 132,133p
function extractVerdict(comments: string[], valuePattern: RegExp, missingLabel: string): VerdictExtraction {
  const clearHits = comments.filter((c) => valuePattern.test(firstThreeLines(c)))
```

Line 133 drops from the candidate set any comment whose `VERDICT:` sits below line 3. Round 4 narrowed where a verdict's **value** is read; it did not say a comment may vanish.

One commit:

1. Candidate set = every comment with a `VERDICT`-shaped line anywhere in its body (whole-body test, the pre-round-4 pattern). Value = read from the first three lines only. A candidate whose first three lines carry no value is `DANGLING` with `danglingNote` set, never skipped: most-recent-candidate-wins runs over the candidate set, so a later unclear comment beats an earlier clean `PASS`.
2. Tests, one each: `extract([A, B])` with A = line-1 `VERDICT: PASS` bound to head, B = later same-head comment with `VERDICT: FAIL` on line 4 → result is `DANGLING`, gate blocks; `extract([A])` → head-bound `PASS` unchanged; `extract([B])` → `DANGLING`.
3. `bun run test`, `bun apps/cli/src/index.ts pr report --push 392`, one `Head:` comment, stop.

body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-6 -->
Principal ruling, round 6, on #issuecomment-5522871874 (head `67108c12`). F1 confirmed by reading, not by trusting the comment:

```
$ git show origin/task/review-convergence-v1/2:apps/cli/src/commands/review-post.ts | sed -n 1033,1035p
  const nonBlocking = findings.filter((f) => !blockingSeverities.includes(f.severity))
  const changedRanges = computeChangedRanges(pr, judgedHead, resolvedHead)
  const outside = findingsOutsideDelta(nonBlocking, changedRanges)
```

`missingPriorIds` (line 601) demands every prior id in the file; `findingsOutsideDelta` (656) then refuses any non-blocking one whose location is outside the delta. Carried ids are never new scope; they are the record. The gate contradicts itself on every round two whose fix is smaller than the prior findings' footprint — which is every round two.

**One commit, no new mechanism:**

1. F1 — `checkRoundTwo` applies the delta filter to **new** ids only: `findingsOutsideDelta(nonBlocking.filter(f => !priorIds.includes(findingIdState(f.description)?.id)), changedRanges)`. Two tests: (a) prior `F1`–`F3` restated with states at locations outside the delta → accepted; (b) a new non-blocking `F4` outside the delta → refused with the existing message. No other line in that function changes.
2. F3 — `aeg-root/roles/reviewer.md:74`: the advisory-`scope`-MINOR sentence gains the clause "on round one; on a re-review, `vinaya review post` refuses a new non-blocking finding outside the delta (see below)". Nothing else on that line.
3. F5 — four sites still carry the retired bracket form; each becomes the outcome form (`--escalate <authority|strategy|product>`, "an escalation is its own outcome, never a finding"):
   ```
   $ git grep -n "\[ESCALATE\]" origin/task/review-convergence-v1/2 -- aeg-root
   aeg-root/process.md:224
   aeg-root/roles/developer.md:266
   aeg-root/state-machine.md:152
   aeg-root/state-machine.md:236
   ```
4. F8 — delete the stale duplicate JSDoc block the reviewer names.
5. F6 stays: `pr-body-frozen` is `main`'s trailing-newline hash (PR #393 addendum 4); this PR takes it by rebase after #393 merges.
6. `rm -rf apps/cli/dist && bun run test`, `bun apps/cli/src/index.ts pr report --push 392`, one `Head:` comment, stop.

Doctrine note for the record, folded into task 8 (#381), no new task: rounds 3–6 of this PR reviewed mechanism that my own rulings added mid-review (delta scoping, evidence file, head fetch), not the brief's surface. A fix commit may add no mechanism beyond what the finding names; a finding whose fix needs new mechanism is escalated into the next task's brief.

title: [review-convergence-v1] 10 — brief-shape refuses a file-and-line reference outside a premise pin or a fenced command
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-2 -->
Principal ruling, round 2. One commit, then one comment `Head: <sha>`, then stop. No further review pass: the Principal reads the diff and merges on the go.

1. Rule (ii): the output block is the fence immediately following the command block, and it must not itself start with a command word; a later fence does not satisfy an earlier command block. Fixture: three command blocks and one trailing output fence fail.
2. `doctrine-no-procedures`: a fence carrying a language tag other than none, `sh`, `bash`, `shell` or `console` is not a command block. Fixture: a ```ts block with two `export` lines passes.
3. Consumer enumeration reads every workspace glob from the root manifest (`apps/*` and `packages/*`), so `apps/cli` counts as a consumer of `@attalabs/aeg-core`. Fixture: a §4 naming `packages/aeg-core/src/x.ts` without an `apps/cli` test path fails.
4. `enforcement.md`: the `brief-shape` row says the three rules run in CI and in `verify-brief.ts` alike; `verify-brief.ts` composes the same `checkBriefSections` with the same consumer enumeration, or the row says which entry point lacks which rule.
5. Grandfathering, by ruling: the three new rules apply to PR bodies opened after this PR merges. This PR's own body predates them; its `brief-shape` red is not a defect of this PR and requires no body edit.

The missing `--evidence-file` on `review post` is item 2 of PR #392's round-four ruling; not this PR.

author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:round-2-addendum-2 -->
Addendum 2 to the round-two ruling. The `CI` workflow's Test step is red at `978e3757` for a reason unrelated to the brief rules; it stays red after addendum 1 unless this lands in the same commit.

**Cause, as run.**

```
$ git ls-files -s apps/cli/src/checks/bin | grep -v '^100755'
100644 36b8dc1df65c2f6b6ec503ff138299764384abf4 0	apps/cli/src/checks/bin/check-doctrine-no-procedures.ts
```

On Linux with no `apps/cli/dist` (what `CI` checks out), the pre-commit hook the quickstart test installs runs `check --all --diff-only` from source and the runner spawns that file directly:

```
✗ doctrine-no-procedures: error (1ms)
    error: Could not run check "doctrine-no-procedures": EACCES: permission denied, posix_spawn '.../apps/cli/src/checks/bin/check-doctrine-no-procedures.ts'
```

so `Chore: install Vinaya` is refused, the log has one commit, and both quickstart tests fail at `quickstart.test.ts:212` with `Expected: 2 / Received: 1` — the exact lines in the CI log. Same tree, same Linux, after `chmod +x` on that one file: `27` checks pass, `2 pass 0 fail`.

Why your local `bun run test` was green: `apps/cli/dist/checks/bin/` exists in your worktree (git-ignored, 29 files, all `+x`), and `apps/cli/src/checks/registry.ts:30` prefers `dist` when present, so the source file's mode is never exercised locally.

**Commit, one, on top of the addendum-1 items:**

1. `git update-index --chmod=+x apps/cli/src/checks/bin/check-doctrine-no-procedures.ts` (and `chmod +x` the file on disk).
2. A test in `apps/cli/tests/` that runs `git ls-files -s apps/cli/src/checks/bin` and fails on any entry not `100755` — the refusal this PR lacked, independent of `dist`.
3. `apps/cli/tests/quickstart.test.ts:212` and `:543`: `expect(log.split('\n').length, out).toBe(2)` — the captured output becomes the assertion message, so the next such failure prints the hook's refusal in the CI log instead of `Received: 1`.
4. Before pushing, prove it the way CI runs it:
   ```
   rm -rf apps/cli/dist && bun run test
   ```
   and paste the summary line in the Head comment.
5. Then addendum 1 unchanged: `bun apps/cli/src/index.ts pr report --push 393`, one comment `Head: <sha>`, stop.

```

## Security

**S1 HIGH `resolved`** — `check-pr-body-frozen.ts`: added `author` to the `gh pr view --json` field list and gated the exemption on `isChangesetsReleasePr(headRefName, author, resolveReleaseActor(loadTrustAnchorConfig()))`, branch-tested first so the trust-anchor round-trip is not paid on every ordinary PR; new test `check-pr-body-frozen-release.test.ts` runs the same body, comments and branch under both authors — release actor gives `info`/exit `0`, a non-release author fails.

**S2 MEDIUM `resolved`** — `review-gate.ts` docstring now states both limits, the moved-base semantic conflict and the whitespace one (`git patch-id --stable` ignores whitespace, so a whitespace-only push keeps the verdict and any non-whitespace content change does not); the same sentence is added to the one-liner in `reviewer.md` and `security.md`. No code change.

**S3 MEDIUM `resolved`** — `check-test-plan.ts` now fetches `body` alongside `comments` and compares the fetched body's authored region to `PR_BODY`'s through `authoredRegion`; on a mismatch the count is `0` and the message says the two env vars describe different pull requests. New test `check-test-plan-identity.test.ts` covers both directions, including that a tick/anchor difference between the two reads is normalised away rather than read as a mismatch.

**S4 LOW `resolved`** — `review-status.ts`: `developerAnswered` now filters with `isPrincipal(author, principalAllowlist)`, the same way the verdict scan above it does; test added proving a non-allowlisted commenter's round marker no longer clears the `stale` pause.

**S5 LOW `resolved`** — `doctrine.ts`: alias lookup is `Object.hasOwn(ROLE_ALIASES, requested) ? ... : requested`; test added for `--role constructor` producing the ordinary "not a known role" refusal instead of a crash.

## Code

**C1 BLOCKER `resolved`** — `enforcement.md`: the writer-side half of the fixed-position rule is deleted. The rule is now the fixed read window the gate actually implements, which is what `reviewer.md` and `security.md` already say. No other sentence in that paragraph changed.

**C2 MAJOR `resolved`** — both archive docstrings reworded: the author is fetched and carried no further, because no `aggregateTaskTokenRows` call site exists in either shim, so the provenance path still reads comment bodies alone.

**C3 MAJOR `resolved`** — `pr-body-381.md` replaced with this PR's body fetched verbatim from the forge, and the docstring rewritten to describe what it actually is rather than claiming "at open, byte for byte". Two assertions moved with it: the captured body carries real ticks, so with zero round comments it fails as `pending` — the evidence gate firing ahead of the unticked-box report — and falls through to the ordinary unticked-box path once a round comment exists. The capture includes the `[principal]` tick that landed on the PR; it is preserved, not normalised away.

**C4 MAJOR `resolved`** — `review-status.ts` prints `behind main: unknown — fetch origin/<base> first` when `behindBy` returns `null`, so a non-zero exit is never paired with a bare `CONTINUE`; test added with a `git` stub that fails `rev-list`. The command's own docstring, the README row and the `COMMANDS` row are updated to match.

**C5 MINOR `resolved`** — the duplicated "own corpus" block deleted from `check-exec-bits.test.ts`; `bin-permissions.test.ts` already owns that assertion.

**C6 MINOR `resolved`** — the session-narrating sentence deleted from `developer.md`'s post-open sequence; the item keeps its second sentence, which states the obligation without narrating.

## Notes

No box ticked this round. The `[agent]` boxes ticked in round `1` cover items whose evidence is unchanged by this commit; item `5` stays unticked (still no verdict to bind), and the `[principal]` box is not mine.

Two of these — S3 and C4 — are cases where the honest fix was to make an unknown say so out loud rather than to guess. S3 treats a body/number mismatch as zero evidence instead of crediting a tick with a comment from another PR; C4 prints that the distance is unmeasurable instead of printing nothing and exiting non-zero. Both are the same shape as the `pending` field this task adds.

Objectives
O1. vinaya issue objectives edit <n> --add "<sentence>" | --drop O<k> | --replace O<k> "<sentence>" --reason "<text>" rewrites the Issue's ## Objectives section through the validated forge-write path, renumbers nothing that exists, and posts one comment on the Issue marked <!-- aeg:objectives:v<k> --> carrying the previous list, the new list and the reason. O2. vinaya pr rule <pr> --file <ruling.md> posts the file as a comment marked <!-- aeg:principal:ruling:<pr>-<k> -->, refuses a body carrying the verdict grammar in its first lines, and prints the comment url. The two contradict on a real drop. Implement --drop as: remove the line, run objectivesOf on the result, and if the parser refuses, refuse the command with the parser's message plus the note that dropping never renumbers; then STOP per §10 so the Principal rules on the grammar. --add appends O<max+1>; --replace keeps the id and changes the sentence.
The validated write path. apps/cli/src/commands/issue.ts's issueEditCommand runs locateBodyOrRefuse → validateTaskIssue (all Issue gates, checkIssueObjectives included) → ensureTrancheLabelExists → runGhWrite(['issue', 'edit', ref], ...). Commands never call commands (apps/cli/specs/surface.md), so your command cannot import issueEditCommand. author: daniboomerang
body:
Head: `a6368c13c9d324f0ee175a84a94b001574d7924f`
<!-- aeg:developer:round-1 -->

Addressed, code review + security, both passes:

**BLOCKER (code review) — spread-order forgery.** Fixed: `{ ...header, ...e }` → `{ ...e, ...header }` in `log-sink.ts`. Header now always wins; added a regression test that forges `subject`/`meta` on the event via `as never` and confirms the trusted, environment-derived values still land in the written line.

**HIGH (security) — path traversal via unsanitized owner/repo.** Fixed: added `isSafeRepoSegment` in `log-sink.ts`, applied to `resolveRepo()`'s result before it reaches `mkdirSync`/`openSync` or `meta.repo`. An owner/repo failing the check (contains `/`, `..`, or anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`) now falls back to the same `unresolved`/`meta.repo: null` path already used for a `null` `resolveRepo()`. Two new tests: a `../../../../../../tmp/evil`-shaped repo, and a bare `/`-containing one.

**MAJOR (code review) / LOW (security) — TOCTOU on the append.** Fixed: replaced the `lstatSync`-then-`openSync` pair with a single `openSync(path, O_WRONLY|O_APPEND|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK)` + `fstatSync` on the already-open descriptor — the same open-then-`fstat` shape `metering-io-guard.ts` already uses on the read side, reused rather than re-derived. Rotation reopens fresh under the same guarded open. The existing symlink-refusal test still passes unmodified against the new implementation.

**HIGH (security) / MAJOR (code review) — redaction gaps.** Rewrote `redact.ts`: added the missing `ghs_`/`ghu_`/`ghr_` GitHub prefixes, AWS access key IDs, Slack tokens, Stripe keys, Anthropic/OpenAI keys, npm tokens, JWTs, PEM blocks, and basic-auth URL credentials — plus a keyword-anchored classic-40-hex-PAT pattern and a keyword-anchored generic `secret=`/`password=`/… pattern. Both keyword-anchored patterns are deliberate, not an oversight: a bare 40-hex string is shape-identical to a git commit sha, and this schema's own `subject.sha`/`meta.doctrine` fields legitimately carry one — blind matching would have redacted those. 16 new test cases, including two explicit negative controls (`doctrine: aeg-root@<sha>` and a bare `run_id` UUID) proving that collision was checked, not assumed.

**MINOR — `Number('')` parsing as `0`.** Fixed in `envelope.ts`: `issueFromTask`/`roundFromEnv` now guard the empty string explicitly, not just `undefined`.

**MINOR — fire-and-forget flush guarantee.** Left as designed. `log()` has zero real callers today (`dispatchRole`/`devReviewLoop` land in a later task per this task's own Boundary); a flush-before-exit mechanism belongs with whichever chokepoint first needs it, not speculatively added here against no real caller.

**MINOR — "two changesets" phrasing.** The PR body is frozen after open, so noting the correction here rather than editing it: `.changeset/vinaya-log-sink.md` is one file declaring version bumps for both `@attalabs/aeg-core` and `@attalabs/vinaya` — the same shape `#423`'s own changeset uses. title: [plan-brief-v1] 1 — The Issue carries every judgment section of the brief; brief render refuses on a gap
author: daniboomerang
body:
Head: c6040099769a71b4cb150cf0e981590e8a9c7ece

<!-- aeg:developer:round-2 -->

`AEG:EVIDENCE` regenerated at this head via `vinaya pr report --push 438`.

## Security review

**Fixed — MEDIUM, fence-breaking (#3).** `renderSection9` spliced Issue-sourced `facts.testPlan.lines` between a *fixed* three-backtick fence. The Issue's own `## Test plan` can itself be fenced with more than three backticks, so a literal ` ``` ` line survives inside `extractFencedBlocks`'s parsed content as ordinary text — splicing that into a fixed fence closed the section early and spilled the rest as unfenced prose. `renderSection9` now computes a fence one backtick longer than the longest run its own lines contain (`safeFence`, `packages/aeg-core/src/brief-render.ts`). New test proves it: a Test plan whose lines contain an embedded ` ``` ` pair widens to four backticks and the injected content stays inside, unbroken (`packages/aeg-core/src/brief-render.test.ts`, "widens its fence rather than let embedded backticks... break out of it"). Full suite green after the fix.

**Traced, not changed — LOW, ReDoS consistency (#4).** Read every new regex in `issue-validation.ts` by hand: `ISSUE_PART_LINE_RE`, `UNIT_TESTS_ONLY_SENTINEL_RE`, `ISSUE_PRINCIPAL_LINE_RE`, `looksLikeFilePath`'s regex. None has the nested-quantifier or restart-from-every-position shape that made `hasBacktickedPath` a linear scan instead of a regex in the first place (a two-wildcard scan separated by a literal, PR #423, MEDIUM) — each is a single greedy/lazy group anchored to a line, linear in input length. The linear-scan helper (`partHasBacktickedPath`, duplicated from `objectives.ts`) exists specifically for that one vulnerable shape; no other new regex shares it, so no change made here.

**Acknowledged, no action (#5).** Confirmed: no `eval`, no new runtime deps beyond the changeset's own devDependency-free diff.

**Not resolved by me — escalating to the Principal, severity: architecture (#1, #2).** Confirmed both findings by tracing the actual call path, not taking them on faith:

- #1 (HIGH) is real: `facts.testPlan.lines` — Issue-body text — is now what `renderSection9` puts in a brief's §9, and `vinaya pr report`'s Group C already executes whatever fenced commands sit in a PR body's own Test Plan section, from the PR head, unattended. Before this task, §9 was one of two hardcoded templates (`bun test <path>` or `bunx turbo test --affected --force`); after it, an Issue's own `## Test plan` fenced content reaches that execution step without any content-safety check beyond `checkTestPlan`'s shape-only presence check. This is not a regression I can fix by inventing an allowlist or a confirmation gate inside this diff — that is exactly the trust-boundary call the brief's own dispatch (Issue #426's Origin note) already made once, collapsing the Brief-Author-as-human-reviewer step for a different, workflow reason, without weighing this consequence. Whether Issue-edit access should be treated as execution-trust, and what gate (if any) belongs between them, is a product/architecture decision I'm not making unilaterally. Escalating as directed — `severity: architecture`, routed to the Principal.
- #2 (MEDIUM) is real but not new in kind: Parts/Surface/Stop-conditions text was already free Issue-body prose flowing into a brief an agent executes on, the same way the eight existing rationale fields (Boundary, Traps, Docs to keep coherent, …) already do. This task widens the volume of such text, not the class of exposure. Noted for the same architecture decision above, not treated as this diff's own defect.

## Code review

**Fixed — MAJOR, unbound doctrine claims.** Eight new sentences across `aeg-root/contracts/planner-brief.md` (4, one per new table row), `aeg-root/templates/brief-template.md` (4, one per placeholder), plus `aeg-root/roles/planner.md`, `apps/cli/README.md` and `packages/sources/src/commands.ts`, stated what `renderBrief`/`renderSection9`/`renderPartCitation`/`brief.ts`'s refusal path do with no `AEG:CLAIM` marker (`roles/reviewer.md`'s doc-correctness rule, #437 — landed just before this task's dispatch, not in my premise pins). Each now carries a marker binding it to the exact function/line it describes. `bun packages/aeg-core/bin/verify-docs.ts` (full mode): `C8 doc-claim: 48 binding(s) verified` — up from the 40 already on `main`, one per new sentence, all resolving true.

**Disclosed, not silently fixed — BLOCKER, vacuous Test Plan evidence.** Confirmed by actually running it:

```
$ bun apps/cli/src/index.ts brief render plan-brief-v1 1 --surfaces 'packages/aeg-core/src/issue-validation.ts'
(stdout empty, exit 1)
stderr: refused — cannot render — missing fact(s): Surface, Parts, Test plan, Stop conditions
$ grep -c '\[named explicitly' <that empty stdout>
0
(grep exit 1)
```

The real Issue #426 was never retrofitted with the four new sections — its body still ends at the eight-field rationale plus `## Origin`. So the third Group-C line's `→ 0` is true for the wrong reason: `grep -c` on empty input prints `0` regardless of whether a real placeholder-free brief was ever rendered. This PR body is frozen post-open (`roles/developer.md`) — I'm not hand-editing the Test Plan section — so the correction lives here: **that line's evidence should be read as proving the refusal path fires correctly on a real, unretrofitted forge Issue, not as proving O2/O3's zero-placeholder claim.** The actual O2/O3 proof — a fixture Issue carrying all four sections, rendered, checked for zero `[named explicitly`/`[NEEDS CLARIFICATION`, and run through `checkBriefSections` end-to-end — lives in `packages/aeg-core/src/brief-render.test.ts`'s `describe('renderBrief — end-to-end from a real Issue body (#426 fixture)')` block (three tests, all green in this PR's own evidence run).

**Decision, surfaced now (should have been in the original body):** `renderBrief`'s missing-fact checks for `Surface`/`Parts`/`Test plan`/`Stop conditions` are deliberately **not** gated by `BRIEF_SECTIONS_SINCE_ISSUE` — the brief's own Part 3 Defeat cases said so explicitly ("an Issue below the cutover with no sections — the render still refuses, because a brief needs them"). The consequence, stated plainly: as of this PR, `vinaya brief render` refuses for **every currently-open task Issue**, not only ones below the cutover — none has the four sections yet, since the grammar didn't exist before this PR. This is a real, immediate availability change to an existing command, intentional per the brief, not something I'm asking to revert — but it belongs in a Decision, and didn't get one until this comment. Whether Issue #426 (and any other in-flight Issue someone wants to run `brief render` against) gets retrofitted is a Planner action, out of this task's Boundary; I did not edit the live Issue myself.

Re-review requested on this head.

**1. MAJOR — run_id-only correlation, fixed.** `hasOwnDispatchLine`/`waitForDispatchLine` now match on `effect_id` in addition to `run_id`+`kind`+`event`. Confirmed: a nested dispatch really does inherit its parent's `VINAYA_RUN_ID` unchanged (createLogSink's own `runId = deps.env().VINAYA_RUN_ID || randomUUID()` picks the inherited value straight back up), so two concurrent dispatches can legitimately share one run_id — `effect_id` (generated once per `dispatchRole` call) is the value actually unique per invocation. Added a regression test (`dispatchRole — a shared run_id`) that runs two concurrent dispatches under an explicitly shared `VINAYA_RUN_ID` and asserts every line is unambiguously attributable to its own call via `effect_id` despite the shared `run_id`.

**2. MAJOR (doc-correctness) — fixed.** The three attribution sentences in `developer.md`/`reviewer.md`/`security.md` now each carry two `AEG:CLAIM` markers binding them to `dispatch.ts`'s child-env assignment and `envelope.ts`'s `unattributed` fallback. (developer.md's sentence also moved from `## The short version` to `## Reference` — C7 scans the former literally, comments included, and flagged the repo-path citations inside the markers themselves; reviewer.md/security.md's placement was already outside C7's scanned section.)

**3. MAJOR — exit code not in the persisted line: confirmed, not fixable inside this task's surface.** Re-checked the merged `DispatchEventSchema` again: no `exit_code` field exists on any dispatch-family event, and `payload` is `z.object({}).strict()` — it structurally cannot carry an extra key. There's no field to smuggle it into without either lying in an existing field or editing `packages/aeg-core/src/log/schema.ts`, which this brief pins as out of surface ("consumed, unchanged — no new family, no schema edit"). This stays exactly as disclosed: `DispatchHandle.exitCode` is real and returned to the caller; the persisted line cannot carry it until a follow-up task adds the field. Not something I'll silently work around by editing aeg-core off-brief.

**4. MAJOR — hand-typed clean-run claim, acknowledged but not fixed by editing the body.** The finding is correct: that sentence asserted a test count outside the Evidence block, which the doctrine's own "evidence is emitted, never typed" rule forbids. Per the same doctrine, the PR body is written once at open and I don't hand-edit it afterward for anything outside the `AEG:EVIDENCE`/`AEG:TOKENS` anchors — so I'm not rewriting that paragraph in place. For the record: the claim was true when written (confirmed by two full local runs) and remains true now (the pre-push hook — a real, mechanically-enforced gate that refuses the push on a failing run — just ran the untruncated suite clean at this head, `1599 pass, 0 fail`, though per the same rule that number is prose here too, not emitted evidence). That is not "the same recovery," and I mischaracterized it as such. The forge comment's *content* is accurate (the real, originally-dispatched brief, reformatted so the mechanical grader can read it), but the claim that reaching it matched the tool's own suggested path was wrong. New tests cover: refusal before any render/comment-check/post when unauthorized, fail-closed on an unresolvable identity, and confirmation the check is never consulted when `--agent` is omitted.

**MAJOR — `checkSummaryDensity` permanently dormant from this task's own heading rename.** Fixed, not just noted: renamed to `checkDecisionsDensity`, targeting `## Decisions` (the heading this task's own template rename introduced) instead of the retired `## Summary`. The enforced property is unchanged — exactly one blank-line-delimited block — which still holds for Decisions' bullet-list shape (no blank lines between items = one block) while still catching padding with a second, separately-blocked paragraph. New test asserts a real, non-empty `promptFile` string reaches the call.

**[BLOCKER] `resolveObjectivesSource`/`hasObjectivesHeading`/`objectivesOf` searched the RAW PR body** — a no-Issue PR following this repo's own deliverable template (full brief pasted inside a collapsed `<details>` reference-copy block) always carries its own `## Objectives` heading in there, so it was wrongly detected as a live objectives source and `review post` refused instead of rendering a no-objectives verdict.

## Code review — not fixed, needs direction

**[MAJOR] O3 gap: the loop's own objectives read still duplicates the heading-scan regex.** I fixed the narrow, safe part of this — `dev-review-loop.ts`'s `extractObjectivesSection` now calls `objectivesSectionBounds` instead of hand-rolling `/^##\s*objectives\s*$/i` — but `surface-scope` hard-refused that commit: Issue #494's own declared `## Surface` names `apps/cli/src/lib` as `out:`, and `dev-review-loop.ts` lives there. So O3's literal "for the gate, review post and the loop" cannot be satisfied inside this task's own declared Surface as things stand; closing it needs either a Surface amendment to this Issue or a new follow-up task against `apps/cli/src/lib`. **[LOW] `OBJECTIVE_MARKER_LINE` accepted any Unicode decimal digit (`\p{Nd}`), the real grammar (`OBJECTIVE_LINE_RE`) only ASCII `\d`.** Narrowed to `\d` in `body-bare-digits-logic.ts` so the two definitions of "objective marker" agree; test added (`O１２.` — fullwidth digits — is no longer exempted).

<!-- aeg:developer:round-7 -->

Root cause found via last round's diagnostic tracing. The `gh` invocation log showed a call I hadn't anticipated between `issue view --json comments` and `pr view --json mergeable`:

```
api repos/atta-labs/vinaya/contents/vinaya.config.json --jq .content
```

That's `loadTrustAnchorConfig()` reading `principals`/`releaseActor` from the forge (never the local working tree, by design) as part of resolving the frozen brief's principal allowlist inside `fetchFrozenBrief` — a completely ordinary, unrelated round-1-entry read. Every fake `gh` fixture's `if [ "$1" = "api" ]` handler matched this call too, not just the real CI check-runs read (`gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/check-runs`) it was meant to answer — both start with `api`. In the O4 conflict scenario this made `.ci-conclusion-checked` a false positive: `fetchFrozenBrief`'s own legitimate forge read touched the marker, never `waitForGreenGate`. This is exactly why it never reproduced locally (a run from inside my real git checkout resolves the trust anchor without ever calling `gh`) but failed deterministically in CI's checkout (which has no such shortcut).

Fix: narrowed every fake `gh`'s `api` handler to match only URLs containing `check-runs` (`${var#*check-runs} != $var`, the same POSIX substring-check idiom used elsewhere in this file). The trust-anchor read now falls through unhandled and `loadTrustAnchorConfig()` gracefully defaults, matching real-world behavior. Removed the diagnostic-only `gh`-invocation-log tracing and its `console.log` now that it did its job; kept the `gate_result_read` outbox assertion, which was real coverage, not scaffolding.

No production code changed this round — the bug was entirely in the test fixtures.

Per the Principal's ruling on this PR: the Issue's Objectives are the contract, the Boundary sentence marking the hook Out was stale and void. O5, O6, and O7 are implemented below.

## Reviewer findings

1. **[MAJOR] aeg-core needs a per-test top-twenty, not one aggregate figure — FIXED.** `packages/aeg-core`'s twenty slowest test *files* (the finest granularity `vitest`'s own reporter gives — no per-test timing exists in the real CI output beyond that) are now a table in the PR body's "Measured slowest tests" section, ranked, with test counts and durations.
2. **[MAJOR] O2's own body admits the "under half" target isn't met, with no formal escalation — FIXED.** Escalated on [Issue #535](https://github.com/atta-labs/vinaya/issues/535#issuecomment-5643905339) with `severity: strategy`, citing Stop-condition 1 by name and asking the Planner to confirm whether O3's sharding satisfies the real ask. **Per this round's instructions, O2 is now accepted at the measured floor by the Principal — no further action pending.**
3. **[MINOR] Evidence Group C shows local timeouts/failures contradicting "0 fail" — STATE UNCHANGED, still explained, not fixable from this body.** C1/C5 are the evidence harness's own per-command budget on suites that are genuinely long (apps/cli's own measured baseline is `249.70s`). C2's "5 fail" is `vi.mock` (a vitest-only API) breaking under the Test Plan's literal `bun test packages/aeg-core` — the wrong runner for a package whose real script is `vitest run` — a defect in the dispatched Test Plan text itself, which this body cannot edit post-open. Real CI is green for both packages.

## Security findings

1. **[LOW] `aggregate` job has no explicit `permissions` block — FIXED.** Added `permissions: { contents: read }`, matching every other job in `ci.yml`.

## O5, O6, O7 — implemented this round

- **O5**: the generated pre-push hook now runs `bunx biome check` over the files changed since the remote base as its first real step. Report-only (no `--write` — a push can't safely rewrite-and-restage already-made commits). `vinaya upgrade` regenerates it; confirmed via `--dry-run` showing only this one hook's diff.
- **O6**: `apps/cli/src/lib/test-selector.ts` — a real import-graph resolver (`from`/bare/dynamic `import` extraction, the same shape `import-boundary.test.ts` already used; DFS reachability from every test file to a changed file; whole-package granularity for a bare `@scope/name` cross-package import). `test-selector.test.ts`'s first test is the literal Part 5 fixture: two packages, three test files, one changed file, exactly one selected. Measured budget on `apps/cli` (this repo's largest package, `123` test files): the shipped `vinaya-select-tests` bin, full repo scan included, took `151ms`-`192ms` wall time end to end; the underlying function call alone, `47ms`-`109ms`. The hook prints `vinaya pre-push: selected N of M test file(s)` every run.
- **O7**: no `--concurrency=1` anywhere in the new hook — that flag was always a `turbo` flag bounding per-package subprocess fan-out (`#438`); `bun test` itself has no such flag. The new step hands every selected file, across every affected package, to ONE `bun test` invocation. `vinaya doctor` flags the OLD hook (still carrying `--concurrency=1`, still missing Biome/the selector) as drifted via its existing generic diff — confirmed live before running `vinaya upgrade` here.

## A real incident this round, disclosed in full

Building O6's own test coverage surfaced a genuine, severe bug: `apps/cli/tests/lib/remote-base.test.ts` created isolated git fixtures in fresh tmpdirs, but a pre-push hook's own invoking git sets `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` for **this** repo, and those inherited into the test's child `git` calls — silently overriding discovery regardless of the fixture's own directory. A "no remote configured" fixture resolved `@{u}` to this branch's real upstream, and several of the test's own `git commit` calls landed as genuine commits on `task/task-run-v1/20`. Recovered via `git reset --hard` to the last real commit (`baa9c112`) after confirming, via reflog, exactly which commits were fixture noise and that the remote had never received them.

Fixed at two layers: `remote-base.ts`'s own `git()` helper now builds an explicit, `GIT_*`-stripped `env` for every call it makes (a real correctness fix — a mutation of `process.env` after process start does **not** reach `execFileSync`'s default env inheritance on this runtime, confirmed live), and — because the same class of bug exists in at least four other pre-existing test files' own `git()` helpers (`doctor.test.ts`, `init.test.ts`, `tracked-hooks.test.ts`, `upgrade.test.ts`, discovered via the corrupted reflog's own commit messages) — the generated pre-push hook itself now unsets every `GIT_*` variable immediately before running the selected tests, protecting every test uniformly rather than patching each vulnerable helper individually. Both fixes are tested: `remote-base.test.ts` passes under a simulated contaminated environment without touching a decoy repo, and `init.test.ts` has a real-subprocess test proving the hook's own unset snippet works. This push's own affected-suite run (visible above) is the first real, successful, non-corrupting execution of this exact test under the exact hook context that broke it.

body:
Head: 3bbf6c8442929cf325c0af845baa11ba08c86031
<!-- aeg:developer:round-4 -->

## Round-3 findings — both FIXED, pushed at `f6785795`

1. **[HIGH] `xargs bun test` argument injection — FIXED.** `apps/cli/src/lib/artifacts.ts` (both the generator and the installed `.vinaya/hooks/pre-push`) piped the selected test-file list into `xargs bun test` with no `--` separator, so a repo-tracked file named like a bun flag (e.g. `--preload=<module>`) was forwarded as that flag rather than a literal path — `bun test --preload` loads and runs an arbitrary module before tests execute, code execution on the pusher's machine during the hook. Fixed with a trailing `--` before the file list, matching the existing `xargs git add --` precedent one function away. Proven with a real subprocess test (`apps/cli/tests/init.test.ts`, "real subprocess: 'bun test --' really does refuse..."): a fixture file literally named `--preload=./evil.js` executes the preload without `--` and does not with it.
2. **[MEDIUM] `xargs bunx biome check` argument injection — FIXED.** Same defect class, same fix, same call site pattern one line above the bun-test invocation. Verified structurally in the same test file.

Both fixes are also live in this repo's own installed hook: `vinaya doctor` flagged the old hook body as drifted after the generator changed, and `vinaya upgrade --yes` regenerated `.vinaya/hooks/pre-push` to match — confirmed via `--dry-run` showing only that one file's diff before applying.

The Reviewer's two round-4 MINOR findings (Biome not literally the hook's *first* line — it follows the pre-existing doctrine gate; the O7 test proves single-process safety and greenness, not literal concurrent wall-clock timing) are both correct as observed and already the exact, disclosed shape O5/O7 ship in — no code change made, no stronger claim stands in the PR body than what those tests actually show.

## O8 — implemented, committed, pushed

`Vinaya Checks` and `Vinaya Body Checks` now trigger on `opened`, `reopened`, `edited` only (`synchronize` removed from both `on:` blocks). A push's own `vinaya pr report --push` always follows with a body edit that already carries the fresh head, firing `edited` — the only trigger either workflow needs. The shared "Fetch PR body" step's `AEG:EVIDENCE`-head catch-up wait loop (and the now-unused `PR_HEAD_SHA` env var) is removed; `evidence-fresh` at the merge gate remains the sole guard against a stale head. Both workflow files were regenerated in this repository via `vinaya upgrade` (confirmed via `--dry-run` first). A new generator test in `apps/cli/tests/init.test.ts` asserts the exact trigger list on both workflows and that the Evidence-head wait is gone. Committed as `41566263`; a follow-up commit `3bbf6c84` reworded one comment that cited an internal tranche slug in product code (`reader-resolvable-prose` refusal) — no behavior change.

## Escalation — `pr report --push`/`pr edit` blocked by a gap in the frozen `aeg:brief:v3` comment itself

`vinaya pr report --push 540` and `vinaya pr edit 540` both refuse with:

```
brief-validation objectives coverage: O8 is not cited by any Part in §6 — every objective must be cited by at least one Part.
```

Checked the frozen brief directly (`aeg:brief:v3`, https://github.com/atta-labs/vinaya/issues/535#issuecomment-5643905339-ish — the v3 comment): its own `## Objectives` section lists `O1`-`O8`, but its own `## 6. Numbered parts` section stops at **Part `6` (`O7`)** — no Part cites `O8`. This is a gap in the frozen brief text itself, not in this branch's diff: `brief-shape` grades the live Issue comment on a real task branch, not the PR body, and the Developer role never re-authors a frozen brief. body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:604-1 -->
Ruling on the HIGH security finding (prose severity cap, `review-policy.ts`).

Facts. `isProseLocation` treats any path under `aeg-root/roles/` as prose. A prose-located finding is evaluated at `PROSE_CAP_SEVERITY = 'MINOR'`, which is not a member of the security scale, so it never blocks under any configured threshold. With `operator.md` shipping authority-grant text, a CRITICAL finding in that text would not block a round. The security reviewer reported this at head `b70660c6`; the developer pinned it with a regression case and requested this decision in the PR body, as this task's brief directs.

Decision. The mismatch is accepted as a known open item for this PR. It is pre-existing, it is pinned by a regression test in this diff, and this task's own brief forbids changing the threshold here: "expose that policy mismatch with a regression case and request an explicit security decision rather than silently changing thresholds." The threshold change belongs to its own task against `packages/aeg-core/src/review-policy.ts`.

This PR is judged on its own objectives. Security recorded O1-O3 MET at `b70660c6`; both reviewer MINORs were fixed and pushed as `d1bdb576`. Reviewers judge at `d1bdb576`.

author: daniboomerang

<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:606-1 -->
Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 4.

Facts. Security reviewed this head and recorded no findings, with O1/O2/O3 MET and no secrets or config-scan issues. The code-reviewer also recorded all three objectives MET, and raised two MAJOR findings:

- `apps/cli/src/lib/dispatch.ts:1676` — `childCommand`/`childStartedAt` are captured immediately after `spawn()` returns, but a vendor CLI installed through a typical npm shebang launcher (`#!/usr/bin/env node`) performs a second exec after the shell resolves it. The recorded identity can therefore describe the launcher rather than the process that survives, which is precisely the case O3's pid-identity check exists to get right.
- `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop/developer-dispatch.ts:742` — `recoverDeveloperLaunch` calls `terminateChildWithGrace` directly rather than through the injected `ReconcileLaunchDeps`, leaving O2's orphan-reap step — the production behaviour this task was opened for — without a test seam.

Neither is a scope question. Both are defects in the mechanism this task delivers: an identity check that misidentifies real vendor CLIs, and an untested reap path, would leave the orphan problem substantially unsolved while appearing fixed.

Decision. The cap is lifted for the rounds needed to address these two findings and re-verify. No other work is authorized under this ruling. Reviewers judge at the head that carries the fixes.

title: [worker-isolation-v1] 2 — Broker task effects using caller-bound operation grants
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:616-1 -->
Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 2.

Facts. Both reviewers recorded O1/O2/O3 MET, and both raised findings that bear directly on what this task delivers:

- MAJOR, `apps/cli/src/lib/broker.ts:73` — `InvocationContext` is a plain unbranded `{role, task}` object carrying no marker that it came from `authenticateWorkerInvocation` or `authenticateOperatorInvocation`. `requestEffect` therefore trusts any context a caller constructs directly, including one that simply declares `role: 'operator'`. O1 is caller-bound grants; an unforgeable context is the mechanism that makes them caller-bound.
- HIGH (security), `apps/cli/src/lib/broker.ts:273` — `isProtectedAdminPath` compares raw strings with `startsWith`/equality and performs no path normalization, so `foo/../.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `./.github/x` or an absolute `/aeg-root/x` evade the protected-path check.
- MAJOR, `apps/cli/src/lib/pr-report-engine.ts:721` — an unrelated `writeTokensBlock` section-boundary fix, with its test changes, is bundled into this task with no connection to O1, O2, O3 or to `broker.ts`, `dispatch.ts` or `isolation.md`.

The first two are defects in the authority mechanism itself: a grant system whose context can be forged, and a protected-path check that normalization defeats, would read as complete while not holding. The third is scope that does not belong in this task.

Decision. The cap is lifted for the rounds needed to address these three findings and re-verify. Brand or otherwise make `InvocationContext` unforgeable at its construction sites; normalize paths before the protected-path comparison; and remove the unrelated `pr-report-engine.ts` change from this task's diff, to be carried by its own task if it is wanted. No other work is authorized under this ruling.

Reviewers judge at the head that carries the fixes.

title: [control-store-v1] 4 — The existing loop recovers budgets and held results from control state
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:617-1 -->
Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 2.

Facts. Round 1 raised a BLOCKER and a matching security HIGH at `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop.ts:964`: a corrupt `loop_state` control-store record throws from inside `runDevReviewLoopBody`'s setup code, which sits outside that function's own try block (the try begins much later, at line 1708). The throw therefore escapes uncaught rather than being handled as the decided pause every driver-path failure is meant to become. Round 1 also raised a MAJOR on the PR body's own Group C evidence, where command C2 recorded `[exit 1]` with a `closes-n` failure while the Test plan claimed it exits `0`.

Round 2 raised a further security HIGH at `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop/round-assess.ts:311`: `persistLoopState` swallows every write failure in a bare catch, and `dev-review-loop.ts:715-723` then treats an absent loop-state record as `infrastructureRetries=0` when deciding whether `--resume` may proceed — so a silently failed write reads as a clean slate.

These are defects in the recovery machinery this task delivers. An uncaught throw on the driver path is the failure class this milestone has spent the night chasing: it ends a driver with no decided pause and no trace. A write failure that is swallowed, then read as zero retries, makes resume decisions on state that was never persisted.

Decision. The cap is lifted for the rounds needed to address the outstanding findings — the uncaught corrupt-state throw, the swallowed `persistLoopState` failure and its `infrastructureRetries` consequence, and the PR body's Group C evidence discrepancy — and to re-verify. No other work is authorized under this ruling.

Reviewers judge at the head that carries the fixes.

title: [worker-isolation-v1] 4 — Reviewers inspect one immutable candidate with isolated scratch space
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:618-1 -->
Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 2.

Facts. Security review raised four HIGH findings and one MEDIUM, all in `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop/reviewer-isolation.ts` — the module this task delivers:

- `:67` — `copyTree` uses `cpSync` with the default `dereference: false`, so a symlink in the developer worktree under review is copied verbatim into the shared read-only candidate and on into each reviewer's tree.
- `:69` — `ISOLATION_COPY_EXCLUDES` covers only `.git`, `node_modules` and `.worktrees`. `copyTree` honours neither the repository's `.gitignore` nor any secret-bearing filename such as `.env`, so untracked secrets in a developer worktree are copied into the shared candidate.

Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 2.

Facts. Review raised findings that bear directly on this task's objective — that a persisted human decision resumes or cancels only its intended run:

- HIGH, `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop.ts:2711` — a concurrent duplicate or replayed `--cancel` reaches `resolveEscalation`'s `acquireOwnership` before its own `consumeResolutionOnce` discovers the replay, so it still bumps the task's control-store ownership epoch. A replayed decision must not move state it was already consumed for.
- MAJOR, `:2727` — `cancelDevReviewLoop` passes the operator-typed `--agent` flag straight into `terminateInFlightLaunchesOnShutdown` with no cross-check against the run's actually dispatched agent, which is never persisted for comparison. A mistyped or stale agent value therefore decides what gets terminated.
- MEDIUM, `packages/aeg-core/src/control-store/local.ts:605` — `writeEscalation` performs a plain overwrite keyed only by `escalationId`, rather than an exclusive create, so a resumed round that re-pauses at the same round and head silently replaces the earlier record.
- MEDIUM, `apps/cli/src/lib/task-tools/read.ts:168` — `readEscalationPacket`, the only function backing the `task_escalation_read` tool, still reads the ephemeral `pause-state.json` and never calls the new `readEscalationRecord`/`readEscalation` control-store path this task introduces. The tool therefore does not see what the task now persists.

Taken together these are defects in the decision-routing mechanism itself, not scope questions. A cancel that acts on the wrong run, or a tool that reads a superseded source, would leave the objective unmet while the tests pass.

Decision. The cap is lifted for the rounds needed to address the HIGH, the MAJOR and both MEDIUMs, and to re-verify. The MINOR coverage gap may be closed in the same round at the Developer's discretion. No other work is authorized under this ruling.

Ruling on the `no_progress` pause at round 4.

**Decision: continue. Dispatch the developer on round 4's findings.**

**Facts.** Round 4's reviewers both returned REQUEST-CHANGES at head `1b73479771a600b7bb237bbd045afb9c013fb4f0`, and the code review and the security review independently reached the same two BLOCKERs on the same two lines:

A confined worker therefore cannot resolve a hostname, so no confined dispatch can reach a model runtime. O3 is not met on the declared host.
2. `apps/cli/src/lib/dispatch.ts:2160` — the `--settings` file is written under `GLOBAL_VINAYA_HOME/dispatch-settings`, which is never carved into the profile's writable subpaths. The confined process cannot read or write the settings file the dispatch itself hands it.

Both are real, both are in this task's own Surface, and neither is an environment artifact. The reviewers were right to block.

**On the pause itself.** The `no_progress` guard fired, but its recorded preconditions are absent on this machine: no `round-4-attach-redelivered` marker exists in the outbox, and `deliveredFindings` is `null` in the control store. The pause comment also carried no `detail`, although the emitting branch computes one naming the round and head. The loop's own event stream for the pause window was truncated by the round-end flush before it could be read. I am therefore **not** ruling that the guard was correct — I am ruling that the work in front of it is unambiguous and should proceed. The guard's behaviour is recorded here as a defect to be investigated separately; it is not this task's problem to solve.

**What the developer does now.** Address both BLOCKERs. Do not treat either as a documentation or comment fix: each names a specific line whose behaviour must change. The five lower-severity findings from the same round are carried forward and judged normally. Re-push, and reviewers re-judge at the new head.

**Budget.** This round is not charged. The developer never received round 4's findings — the driver paused before dispatching it — so no developer attempt was spent on them.

**Why the cap was reached.** The round cap exists to stop a task that cannot converge. That is not what happened here. Of this task's rounds, the majority ended in a driver or transport failure rather than in a judgement that the work was deficient:

| round | how it ended | whose failure |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | reviewer's `findings.txt` missing a required `Search:` clause — refused by the parser | reviewer output format |
| 4 | `no_progress`, with neither of its recorded preconditions present on disk | driver guard (filed as #631) |

**The work has converged.** Round 4's reviewers raised two BLOCKERs — `worker-boundary.ts:368` (no DNS route in the generated Seatbelt profile) and `dispatch.ts:2160` (the `--settings` file written outside the profile's writable subpaths). The evidence of convergence exists; what is missing is a verdict on it.

**Scope of this ruling.** The cap is raised for this task only, to 7. It is not raised for the tranche, and it is not a new default. If reviewers judge `4ee56877` and return REQUEST-CHANGES on merits — a genuine finding about the code, not another transport failure — then the remaining budget applies normally and a further pause at the cap should be read as real non-convergence.

**Not charged.** Rounds 3 and 4 are not counted against the raised cap, for the reasons tabled above.

**What happens now.** Dispatch the code reviewer and the security reviewer against `4ee56877`. Judge both BLOCKERs on their merits at that head; nothing in this ruling pre-judges either. The five lower-severity findings from round 4 are carried forward and judged normally.

**Facts.** The driver refuses to continue because the developer's prior launch (attempt 12) ended `cancelled (signal)` before its vendor session was ever bound, so the exact session cannot be resumed and the loop will not silently start a new one. That refusal is correct behaviour and I am not overriding the principle behind it.

**Why a fresh session loses nothing here.** That launch produced no session at all. Its dispatch output file, `~/.vinaya/dispatch-output/1de87d09-688c-4b4c-8aec-bbc0710a0b9a.log`, is **0 bytes**, created at 08:34 and never written to again. The vendor process was gone from the process table while the driver went on printing `still running — 1920s elapsed` for thirty-two minutes. There is no reasoning, no tool call and no partial edit to preserve: the continuity the guard protects does not exist in this instance.

**Operator disclosure.** I killed that driver process after establishing its child was already dead. The `cancelled (signal)` record is a consequence of that kill, not of anything the task or the developer did. The preceding failure was a transient `gh api` error reading the trust-anchor config from the default branch, which is what ended the session before it bound; `gh` is responsive again and the same call now succeeds.

**Where the work stands.** Head `abd07153` is pushed, the worktree is clean with nothing unpushed, and round 7's code review already reported O1, O2 and O3 MET. **Filed separately.** The driver reporting `still running` for a child that has exited is a defect in its own right — the heartbeat measures elapsed wall-clock and never checks that the vendor process is alive, so a dead dispatch is indistinguishable from a working one in the log. title: [driver-lifecycle-v1] 7 — A brief names its normative documentation and the driver enforces that it is read
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:630-2 -->
Ruling on the round-3 security CRITICAL and the `confidence` pause.

**Decision: the residual risk is accepted and recorded. It does not block this task. Resume and proceed to verdicts.**

**The finding is correct.** O2's Documentation Stop-hook gate reads sources and log files that live under the same OS-user home directory the dispatched Developer session's own tools can write. A session willing to fabricate evidence can therefore satisfy the gate without reading anything. Security has raised this in rounds 1, 2 and 3, and it has been right each time. Nothing here disputes the finding.

**It cannot be closed inside this task.** The developer's analysis is sound and I have verified its two load-bearing claims against `apps/cli/specs/isolation.md`: `dispatchRole`'s spawn "still inherits the full parent environment today", and wiring the Worker/Reviewer spawn path to OS confinement is named there as future work. Both the dispatched session and the driver that writes the enforcement state run as the same OS user with full mutual file access. No edit within this brief's declared surface changes that.

I specifically endorse the developer's refusal to ship a partial mitigation. A `PreToolUse` deny scoped to Bash would leave `Write` and `Edit` reaching the same files — relocating the vector while reading as a fix. Committing that would be worse than the documented gap, because it would retire the finding without closing it.

**Where the fix lives.** Process isolation between the Worker and the driver's enforcement state is `worker-isolation-v1 3` (#560), open now as PR #623 and under review at this moment. That task's own round-4 reviewers raised, and its developer fixed, the DNS and settings-path blockers in the confining profile. This gate becomes tamper-resistant when that boundary lands — not before, and not by anything this task can do.

**What is accepted, precisely.** For the period between this task merging and worker isolation landing, the Documentation entry gate is an **honesty mechanism, not a security control**: it establishes that a compliant session read its normative sources, and it does not defend against a session that chooses to fabricate evidence. That is a real limitation and it is accepted deliberately, on the record, as the security review asked. The limitation must remain documented where the gate is described — `aeg-root/roles/developer.md` item 8 and `apps/cli/specs/loop.md` already state it; it stays stated.

**Instruction to reviewers.** Treat this residual risk as accepted by the Principal. Do not re-raise it as a blocker on this task. Judge the remaining objectives on their merits. If the gate has a defect *other* than the shared-user trust boundary — a way a compliant session fails the gate, or an evidence path weaker than the one described — that is a new finding and blocks normally.

**Budget.** No round is charged for the escalation. The developer produced no code change because none was possible within the surface, said so plainly, and escalated rather than looping — which is the behaviour the contract asks for.

title: [task-log-v1] 6 — Task operations, loop transitions and handoffs emit one correlated history
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:638-1 -->
Ruling on the `no_progress` pause.

**Decision: continue. Fix the root cause this round, inside this task's existing Surface. No split, no new task.**

**Facts.** Two rounds of review, both REQUEST-CHANGES/FAIL, on the same root cause: `apps/cli/src/lib/task-tools/server.ts:356`'s `void handleLine(line).then(...)` dispatches concurrent task operations without awaiting or serializing them. Combined with `cancelDevReviewLoop`'s temporary `process.env.VINAYA_TASK`/`VINAYA_RUN` mutation, a concurrent call for a different task can have its own event misattributed. Security's round-2 pass additionally found `resume.ts` and `cancel.ts`'s own `emitOperationEvent` never scope `VINAYA_TASK` at all — every real `task_resume`/`task_cancel` event on the shared server currently misfiles to `none.ndjson`, not only during a race. The round-2 test was flagged as masking this: it manually sets `VINAYA_TASK` before calling `log()`, a shape its own comment incorrectly attributes to the real code path.

**Why this stays inside 566.** `task-tools/server.ts`, `resume.ts` and `cancel.ts` are already inside this task's declared Surface (`apps/cli/src/lib`). This is not new scope — it is the same defect both reviewers named in round 1 and again in round 2, still open. Splitting it into a separate task would mean a second brief, a second dispatch, and a second full review cycle for one fix with one root cause. That is slower, not more careful.

**What the developer does this round.**
1. Serialize `server.ts`'s dispatch — await each `handleLine` call (or otherwise ensure two different tasks' operations cannot interleave) before reading the next line.
2. Scope `process.env.VINAYA_TASK` around `emitOperationEvent`'s `log()` call in both `resume.ts` and `cancel.ts`, the same discipline `cancelDevReviewLoop` and `log-flush.ts`'s `logForFlush` already use.
3. Replace or extend `cancel.test.ts`'s round-2 regression test so it exercises the real code path — not a fixture that sets `VINAYA_TASK` itself — and add a genuine concurrent-dispatch case: two different tasks' operations interleaved through `server.ts`, asserting each event lands under its own task's outbox.

**Not charged.** No round is spent: two prior rounds already narrowed this to one precise, cited defect: the developer is not starting over, it is finishing the fix reviewers have twice pointed at the same three files for.

author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:665-3 -->
**Principal ruling — a shell is not a utility.**

The architecture test is the right instrument and its grandfather list is correct. One hole, both reviewers found it: `sh` and `bash` sit in the safe-utility list beside `git`, `chmod` and `mkdir`. Those three do one fixed thing; a shell runs whatever string it is handed, so a spawn of `bun`, `node` or the CLI hidden behind a shell passes the scan unseen.

It returns a complete `LoopDeps` of fakes backed by one mutable in-memory world (branch and head per round, PR state, gate results, posted comments, role outcomes per round). Every fake reads from and writes to that world, so a state transition such as the head appearing after the Developer's push happens once, in the world, not per fixture. A fixture states only how its scenario differs from the default world.
2. Convert the file's tests to that harness, one `describe` block at a time, with one commit per block. Each converted test keeps every assertion it has today. A test whose subject is process behaviour (exit status, a signal, the driver lock, the start-of-run sweep, stdio shape) stays on a real process with its one-line reason, as the architecture test already requires. Lower that test's ceiling as each block converts.
3. Meet O2 (the file in at most a third of its time before this pull request) and record O4 (the file's own time and a pre-push run, before and after).

The only remaining stop is a test that cannot move in-process without a new dependency seam in production code outside `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop.ts`. A seam inside that file is allowed, and `apps/cli/specs/loop.md` is updated with it.

title: [unattended-run-v1] 22 — A pause recorded before its pull request existed can be cancelled and resumed: the catalog records no pull request as none, and rulings come from the Issue
author: daniboomerang
body:
Round 2 response — pushed as `193d4f13`.

## Fixed

**F1 (BLOCKER) / F2 (MAJOR) — the continuation now uses the address form that works.** Verified the claim first: `assembleAndRenderBriefForIssue` refuses an Issue carrying a `vinaya/tranche:*` label (`brief-assembly.ts:680`), that message does not match `ALREADY_DISPATCHED_PATTERN` (`task-run.ts:62`), so the child exits with the ruling already spent. `noPushResumeArgv` (`pause-resume.ts`) now picks between `task run <tranche> <n>` and `task run --issue <n>` from the pause's **own branch** — where `developerBranchFor` already recorded the answer at dispatch, read back by `parseTaskBranchIdentity`. No forge call, and it cannot disagree with the branch the run is on. It is the single builder behind all three namings, which is what the two reviewers' findings had drifting apart: the Issue pause comment, `task_escalation_read`'s `permittedNextActions`, and the argv `defaultResumeLaunch` spawns.

**F3 / security HIGH — the freshness baseline is no longer vacuous.** `bestEffortInputVersions` read the ordinal only off a pull request, so a no-pull-request escalation recorded `0` and `newestIssueRulingOrdinal > 0` was satisfied by any ruling ever posted on that Issue. It now reads `fetchNewestIssueRulingOrdinal(task)` for that case — a new `LoopDeps` field beside its pull-request sibling, so the in-process harness drives it.

**F5 (in-surface half) / security MEDIUM — the marker is named.** No shipped command posts a ruling on an Issue, so the pause comment now prints the `<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:<k>-<n> -->` line and the ordinal to exceed. Neither was guessable before.

**F8 / security LOW — the refusals stopped lying.** Both the replay refusal and the failed-launch refusal claimed a new ruling reopens the escalation. `consumeResolutionOnce` refuses that id forever and an identical pause reuses it (`sameEscalationInstance`), so both now name the command to run directly.

**F6, F7, F9, security LOW-6** — the stale `runDriverLoop` comment, the orphaned doc block, `isLegacyPauseState` rejecting a `null` `prNumber` (which migrated a real pause as `source: 'fresh'` at round `0` with no `paused` transition), and `task-status.ts`'s duplicated pause reader that had silently diverged.

Mutation-checked, not asserted: forcing the `--issue` form fails `7` cases across three files; resetting the ordinal baseline to `0` fails the new escalation-record case; re-requiring a numeric `prNumber` in the migration guard fails the new migration case.

## Not fixed — outside this brief's declared Surface

Both reviewers raised these and both are real. §4 lists `apps/cli/src/commands` and `packages/sources` as `out`, and `surface-scope` refuses a diff that touches them, so I cannot land either without a Surface supersede.

- **F4 / security LOW-4** — `commands/task-run.ts:158` prints `dev-review-loop --resume 0` for this pause. `noPushResumeCommandFor` is exported and takes the branch, so the fix is one line once the Surface allows it.
- **F5 (remaining half)** — `commands/pr-rule.ts` posts only through `gh pr`; an `Issue`-target variant is what would let a Principal authorize this through a command rather than by hand. `packages/sources/src/commands.ts`'s `task run` help text also still names the retired form.

Both are recorded as backlog Issue `#785`, and `apps/cli/specs/loop.md` states them rather than claiming the printed commands work.

## Disclosed, not fixed — a consequence of the brief's own ruling

**security MEDIUM-2** — the relaunched `task run` re-enters at round `1` with the frozen brief; nothing reads Issue rulings into that dispatch, so the ruling's *text* never reaches the resumed developer. The Principal ruling of `2026-09-27` names `task run` as the continuation for this pause, and feeding Issue rulings into a round-1 dispatch is outside `O4`. `apps/cli/specs/loop.md` now says so explicitly under "The Operator's continuation and cancellation", so a Principal knows a ruling that changes the work has to say it where the developer reads. The unbounded-relaunch half of that finding is closed by the `F3` fix: each pause now records a real baseline, so one ruling authorizes one resume.

title: [unattended-run-v1] 22 — A pause recorded before its pull request existed can be cancelled and resumed: the catalog records no pull request as none, and rulings come from the Issue
author: daniboomerang
body:
Round 3 response — pushed as `c3361f83`.

## Fixed

**F1 / security HIGH — the marker named a ruling the gate would always refuse.** Verified the convention first: `RULING_MARKER_ORDINAL = /^<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:\d+-(\d+) -->$/` captures the **second** number, and `pr rule` posts `${prRef}-${k}`. The renderer put the ordinal first and fixed the second at `1`, so a ruling written exactly as the comment instructed parsed as ordinal `1` — refused for every pause whose baseline had reached `1`, which the round-2 real-baseline fix made the ordinary case. `principalRulingMarker(ref, ordinal)` now builds it, declared beside the regex that parses it, so the two cannot drift.

**F3 — the test is the reason the blocker shipped.** The literal compare (`baseline 4` expects `ruling:5-1`) codified the swap. Markers are now asserted by feeding the rendered line back through `newestPrincipalRulingOrdinal` and requiring the parsed ordinal to exceed the baseline — a property no slot arrangement can satisfy accidentally. Applied at all three sites the reviewer named.

**F2 / security F4 — the model travels with the launch.** The spawned argv dropped `--model` while the comment, `permittedNextActions` and both refusals rendered it. The relaunch was therefore re-resolving a model from the Issue's agent-class table rather than running under the one the paused run was dispatched with.

**security F3 — the printed command is the shell encoding of the argv.** The tranche segment is unvalidated forge input (`developerBranchFor` takes it from the Issue title's `[^\]]+`; `parseTaskBranchIdentity` accepts any `[^/]+`) and it lands inside a fenced block a human or an Operator agent is told to run. `noPushResumeCommandFor` now shell-quotes element by element. This also closes the divergence you noted for a whitespace-carrying tranche: the space-join was a second, weaker builder wearing the first one's name.

**security F5 — an unreadable baseline no longer records `0`.** `0` is not a missing value there; it is the claim "this Issue carries no rulings", which a failed read never established. The Issue read now propagates — the caller's own best-effort `try` swallows it, no escalation record is written, and both tools fail closed on machinery that already exists (`task_resume`: "no durable record"; `task_cancel`: `StaleEscalationError`) — while the pause stays continuable by its printed command, which needs no ruling at all. The pull-request branch keeps its permissive `0`, which it always had and which its own gate re-reads.

**security F6 — the last unnormalized writer.** The main round-loop pause site stored `prNumber` raw with no `<= 0` guard on the comment it posts. Unreachable with a non-real value today, as you said, but it left that path's conversion resting entirely on the read side.

**F5 / F6 / DOCS** — the spec wrote the marker with the slots reversed (encoding the same confusion), claimed the model travelled with the argv, said "Four things changed:" above six bullets, and had the two-extra-readers paragraph wedged mid-list. The changeset repeated the two claims that did not hold. All corrected.

Mutation-checked, each against the cases that should catch it: swapping the marker slots back fails `5` cases across two files; space-joining the printed command fails `2`; dropping the model from the launch fails `1`; re-swallowing the Issue baseline read fails `1`.

## F4 / security F2 — still out of Surface, with the executed evidence

I owe a correction: in round 2 I said `surface-scope` refuses this. I then probed it with an **uncommitted** edit and it passed, which would have made that claim wrong. Run against the real derivation it is right — `checkSurfaceScope` reads Issue `#781`'s own `## Surface`:

```
out globs: ["packages/sources","packages/aeg-forge-state","apps/cli/src/commands","apps/cli/src/checks","aeg-root",".github"]
task-run: {"ok":false,"violations":[{"file":"apps/cli/src/commands/task-run.ts","glob":"apps/cli/src/commands"}]}
pr-rule:  {"ok":false,"violations":[{"file":"apps/cli/src/commands/pr-rule.ts","glob":"apps/cli/src/commands"}]}
sources:  {"ok":false,"violations":[{"file":"packages/sources/src/commands.ts","glob":"packages/sources"}]}
```

The earlier pass was an artifact of the check diffing against `origin/main` rather than the working tree. So the fix is one line and mechanically cannot land on this branch: `noPushResumeCommandFor` is already exported and takes the branch. It needs a Surface supersede, or it lands on `#785`. Three rounds have now asked for it — if the Principal would rather it land here, a supersede widening `out:` is the one thing that unblocks it.

title: Fix(cli): `log set-credential` stores nothing, because `security add-generic-password -w` prompts on the terminal instead of reading standard input
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:879-1 -->
**Ruling: the Principal's Test Plan item fails; one more development round.** Storing works: after `log set-credential VINAYA_LOG_TOKEN` the item exists in the login Keychain (service "Vinaya Log"), with no prompt. But the self-test does not look in the Keychain: with `VINAYA_LOG_TOKEN` unset in the environment, `vinaya log selftest` fails with "this host holds no ingest credential", because `logsCredentialMissing` in `apps/cli/src/lib/log-sink.ts` checks only the process environment. Required: `logsCredentialMissing` counts a referenced variable as present when the macOS Keychain holds it (service "Vinaya Log", account = the variable name), through the same Keychain reader the header substitution already uses, injected so tests use a fake; every caller (the self-test and the CI path) gets the same answer. Add a test where the variable is absent from the environment but present in the fake Keychain and the self-test passes the credential check. No other change.

title: Fix(cli): on macOS the always-on sandbox blocks git, loses the Developer session between rounds, and blocks the task log
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:986-1 -->
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:986-1 -->
**Ruling: two more fixes belong in this pull request; the Boundary's "Out" item on the task-tools MCP server is lifted.**

1. **The MCP server's `node` must run inside the sandbox.** A confined Claude or Codex session that starts the task-tools MCP server fails with `EPERM … posix_spawn 'node'`: the `node` it starts resolves to a real path outside the granted directories (on this Mac `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` is a link into `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/<version>/bin/node`; on other hosts it can live under `~/.nvm/versions/node/<version>`). Resolve the real path of the `node` the MCP configuration starts, at launch, and grant read and exec — never write — on its installation directory only. Prove it with a profile-rendering test for both a Homebrew-style and an nvm-style path.
2. **Correct the misleading crash message.** `apps/cli/src/lib/dev-review-loop/round-assess.ts` says a resume "failed this round … after succeeding last round" even in round 1, where no earlier round exists. Say "after succeeding last round" only when a previous round's resume succeeded; otherwise state that the first resume of the session failed.

Both are inside this task's Surface (`apps/cli/src/lib`). Add tests, push, and continue.

title: Fix: every refusal at the driver's publication step goes back to the Developer at once, bounded
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:1023-2 -->
Principal ruling — F1 is valid; fix it this round, then the loop continues.

O7 means "the remote task branch has no commits beyond the default branch", not "its head equals the default branch's head". A branch created at an older default-branch commit is left behind as soon as the default branch advances — exactly how tonight's reruns kept receiving the resume prompt. Executed here:

```
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 75a1efdc origin/main   # exit 0: no commits beyond main
$ [ "$(git rev-parse 75a1efdc)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)" ]   # false: not equal
```

So an equality test misclassifies it. Decide with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <remote branch head> origin/<default>` (exit 0 = commit-free → full first-dispatch brief), add a test for the behind-default case alongside the equal-head one, and correct `apps/cli/specs/loop.md` to state the ancestor rule.

<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:1091-1 -->
Security F1 is accepted: fix it in this round, do not decline it. The sweep now deletes a task folder when its Issue is reported missing, so the Issue lookup must name the repository the folder belongs to.

1. Both `gh issue view` calls in `apps/cli/src/lib/task-sweep.ts` pass `--repo <owner>/<repo>`, taken from the sweep's existing `resolveRepo` dependency.
2. When `resolveRepo` returns null, the sweep treats the Issue as unreadable and keeps the folder. It never deletes without a named repository.
3. Add a test for each: the lookup carries `--repo`, and a null repository keeps the folder.

Checked from a directory outside any repository: `gh issue view 1067 --repo atta-labs/vinaya --json state` returns `{"state":"OPEN"}`, and a missing number returns `GraphQL: Could not resolve to an issue or pull request with the number of 999999.`, which the existing case-insensitive matcher already covers. Use that real text in the test fixture.

title: Fix: a main merge the Developer makes in its turn never puts main's own files into the publication checks
author: daniboomerang
body:
<!-- aeg:principal:ruling:1106-1 -->
The conflict is resolved by one source of truth for the default branch that the Developer cannot forge: the remote itself. This supersedes the brief's trap against fetching, for this one read only.

1. At publication, the driver reads the remote default-branch head with `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`, giving S. When S's object is missing locally, the driver fetches that one ref itself. The Developer never does.
2. A merge parent P is the default branch only when `git merge-base --is-ancestor P S` holds. A commit that merely descends from the default branch (security F1, a side branch cut from it) fails this test, so its paths stay task changes and are judged by the Surface and protected-path checks.
3. The comparison base is the newest merge parent, nearest the head, that passes test 2. A merge whose parent fails the test never moves the base (security F2). The credential scan uses the same base.
4. Keep the stale-ref objective: compare against the exact P that was merged, never the local default-branch ref by name.
5. Tests: a genuine merge of the default branch publishes; a merge of a side branch cut from the default branch with an out-of-Surface edit is refused; a crafted merge cannot move the base.

Checked here: `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` returned the remote head; a commit three behind it passed `git merge-base --is-ancestor`; a commit built on that same commit as a side branch failed it.
